# CRANIAL EPIDURAL ABSCESS

Treatment involves source control by drainage procedure and antimicrobial therapy.

Beta-lactam antibiotics are more effective than vancomycin against susceptible Staphylococci. If Staphylococcus is isolated, once methicillin-resistance is ruled out, switch to an anti-staphylococcal beta-lactam antibiotic. Pseudomonas is a potential pathogen in post-surgical patients or patients with known Pseudomonas colonization.

# Consult Neurosurgery, Neurology, and Infectious Disease

# Duration of Therapy

Treat for 3 to 6 weeks after surgical drainage.

---

References:

- Mandell chapter: Subdural Empyema, Epidural Abscess, and Suppurative Intracranial Thrombophlebitis
- Pradilla et al, Lancet Neurol, 2009, 8(3)292-300
- Up-To-Date Article: Intracranial Epidural Abscess
Therapy:
Preferred if Pseudomonas is not suspected:

Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q12h ($) [M] <AND> metronidazole 15 mg/kg IV q12h

($) [DI] <AND> vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h ($) [R]

Preferred if Pseudomonas is suspected:

Cefepime 2gm IV Q8h ($$) [R] <AND> metronidazole 15 mg/kg IV q12h ($) [DI] <AND> vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h ($) [R]

Alternative:

Assessment of beta-lactam reaction

Meropenem 2 gm IV q8h ($$) R,O <AND> vancomycin 15mg/kg IV q12h ($) R

## Treatment if methicillin-sensitive S. aureus is isolated

Nafcillin 2 gm IV q4h ($$) R,DI

< OR >
Cefazolin 2 gm IV q8h ($) R
